definition: In computer vision, visual descriptors or image descriptors are descriptions of the visual features of the contents in images, videos, or algorithms or applications that produce such descriptions.
details: They describe elementary characteristics such as the shape, the color, the texture or the motion, among others.

explainer.lead: A visual descriptor is a description of the visual features of content in images or videos, or of the algorithms or applications that produce such descriptions. It matters because it captures elementary characteristics used to represent and compare visual content.

tiers.eli5: It's a short summary of what something in a picture looks like—its shape, colour, texture or movement.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use descriptors to encode elementary characteristics such as shape, color, texture or motion. A pitfall is that a descriptor covers only elementary characteristics, so it does not by itself capture everything about the content.
tiers.paperLevel: Visual or image descriptors are descriptions of the visual features of the contents in images or videos, or of algorithms or applications producing such descriptions; they describe elementary characteristics including shape, color, texture and motion.

explainer.example: A descriptor summarizes the color and texture of a region in an image so that content can be described and compared.
